subject: Acme — Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (rate limits / overage)

Thanks for taking the call today — good to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call recap:
- Primary objective: embed Redwood for user-facing summarization and search (high peak traffic during campaign pushes).
- Current ask: baseline monthly token volume estimate + expected burst behavior so we can size quota and recommend pricing.
- Key concerns you raised: predictable unit economics, burst capacity during campaigns, and clear overage terms.

What we need from Acme to finalize a proposal:
1) Typical steady-state tokens/mo (avg).
2) Peak burst TPS or tokens for campaign spikes (how long do spikes last?).
3) Target budget range for inference (monthly).
4) Target unit economics (if you have a target $/1M tokens you want to hit).

What Redwood proposes next:
- I’ll pull together a rate-limit/overage options doc (3 options: conservative quota, burst buffer, and pre-committed additional capacity) and price them against the volumes you provide.
- Rafael (cc’d) can review for a custom burst policy if Acme needs higher short-term capacity.
- If you share the usage CSV you mentioned, I’ll run a quick model and send a pricing worksheet.

Attachments: post-call-deck.pdf (summary), sample overage terms (redwood_overage_terms.pdf).

Proposed next step: send the usage CSV and your budget range by Tuesday and we’ll follow up with a recommended quota + pricing (incl. per-1M token unit and any overage multipliers).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — High-performance, reliable LLM inference for product teams

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (rate limits / overage)

Thanks Marissa — short answers below, putting Priya on-thread to confirm some details.

1) Steady-state tokens/mo: ~120M tokens/mo across our API (this is conservative; could grow 2-3x over 12 months).
2) Peak bursts: Campaign spikes can multiply traffic ~4x for 30–90 minutes, roughly 10–15 times/day during launches. We do a weekly push that causes a 45-minute sustained spike.
3) Budget range: initial monthly budget target is $8k–$18k while we validate the integration. If we see ROI, we can commit higher in Q2.
4) Target unit economics: we’re aiming for roughly $12–$20 per 1M tokens (target $/1M tokens is flexible within that band).

Also: priority question — what does Redwood’s short-term burst policy look like? Can we get a cushion for the 45-minute spikes without pre-committing full capacity? If possible we’d prefer an automated burst buffer with metered overage versus a long procurement cycle.

I’ll attach a sample usage export (acme_usage_report.csv) in a follow-up; want to scrub a couple of fields first.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (rate limits / overage)

Alex — thanks, this is very helpful. A few clarifications and what we’ll propose: 

Clarifications:
- When you say 4x bursts for ~45 minutes, is the 4x relative to the steady-state average (so peaks hit ~480M tokens/mo equivalent for that hour)? Good to confirm so we size the short-term buffer correctly.
- For the weekly push that’s the most important to support without throttling — we can map that to a scheduled burst window.

Preliminary pricing guidance (ballpark):
- Based on the volumes you gave, a standard hosted plan without commitments would land in the ~$20–$28 per 1M tokens range for our top-tier LLM profile.
- If you pre-commit monthly capacity (12–36 month term) and agree to a volume band, we can get to ~$12–$18 per 1M tokens (your stated target band).
- Overage handling: two common options — (A) automatic metered overage billed at 1.25x base unit price (for short bursts), (B) burst buffer add-on (pay-for-reserved-burst capacity) priced as a flat monthly buffer sized to your longest spike (recommended if you want guaranteed non-throttled performance).

Rate-limits / quota suggestions:
- Baseline quota: set at ~150M tokens/mo to cover steady-state + a small cushion.
- Burst policy: allow automated bursts up to 3x baseline for short windows during scheduled campaign periods; overage beyond that billed via (A) metered overage or (B) charge against pre-purchased burst buffer.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Rafael and Camila will review for a formal proposal and confirm whether we can accommodate 4x spikes (we typically allow 3x automated bursts, but we can evaluate temporary exceptions).
2) If you send the CSV, I’ll run the cost model and return a pricing worksheet showing: committed vs. metered options, projected monthly bill, and $/1M token line items.
3) We can also propose a short trial with a temporary increased burst quota so you can validate during your next campaign.

Attaching: redwood_overage_terms.pdf (sample overage terms). I’ll follow up with a formal proposal by Wednesday after Rafael’s review.

Best,

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — Acme burst exception request (ACME-5421)

Rafael / Camila — putting the notes here so we have context for pricing/prod. Acme is asking for 4x sustained bursts for ~45 minutes once a week and smaller repeated spikes during launches. They want to avoid heavy upfront pre-commit.

Numbers: steady 120M/mo, peaks ~4x, target budget $8k–$18k/mo, target $/1M tokens $12–$20. They prefer an automated burst buffer + metered overage vs. committing to a big reserved pool.

Questions for you:
- Can we offer a temporary 4x scheduled burst for the weekly push as an exception for the trial period (30–60 days)?
- If not, can we propose a hybrid: baseline quota at 150M, automated bursts up to 3x, and a small paid burst buffer sized for the 45-minute window (pre-paid in monthly increments)?

If we can do a 30-day scheduled exception, I recommend 1) trial burst quota, 2) meter overage at 1.25x, 3) commit to a follow-up pricing review at end of trial.

Assigning to Rafael to confirm feasibility and Camila for the pricing worksheet. I’ll wait for a quick thumbs-up and then send the formal proposal to Acme.

Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (rate limits / overage)

Appreciate the fast follow-up, Marissa. The proposal outline sounds reasonable. Two quick asks before we proceed: 

1) Can Redwood provide a short trial with the 4x scheduled burst for our weekly push for 30 days? We’ll validate performance and make a go/no-go decision.

2) If you can share the pricing worksheet (committed vs. metered) and an example invoice showing the $/1M tokens math, that’ll help budget sign-off.

If you can get Rafael’s confirmation this week, we’ll plan to run the trial next Monday and share the usage CSV today after scrubbing PII.

Thanks — Alex
